findings.issue_text: [High/bug] handleNewBooking.ts:964 — async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach are not awaited, so rejections escape the try/catch and become unhandled rejections; cancellation failures are silently unreported

[Medium/bug] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:52-56 — reminder.referenceId can be null but is passed directly as SendGrid batch_id, causing a malformed API request that aborts cancellation for subsequent reminders in the loop

[Medium/bug] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-67 — if the SendGrid cancel request throws for one reminder, the whole loop aborts via the catch, skipping cancellation/DB deletion of remaining reminders; failed reminders are never marked or retried so the email still sends

[Medium/bug] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:62 — workflowReminder.delete runs unconditionally right after issuing the async/best-effort SendGrid cancel request, deleting the DB row even if cancellation later fails and the email sends anyway (no reconciliation)

[Medium/bug] emailReminderManager.ts:197 (immediateDelete branch) — reminder is cancelled in SendGrid but the DB row is neither deleted nor marked cancelled, so rows accumulate permanently and the cron query (cancelled: true) never cleans them up

[Medium/bug] smsReminderManager.ts:178 — if twilio.cancelSMS throws, the catch swallows the error and workflowReminder.delete never executes; reminder stays in DB, SMS may still deliver, no retry mechanism, only a console.log

[Medium/concurrency] workflows.tsx:572 — remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) fires async cancels without awaiting, so replacement reminders can be scheduled before old ones are cancelled, allowing duplicates; rejections are also unhandled

[Medium/bug] emailReminderManager.ts — on any error the function logs via console.log and returns without marking the reminder cancelled or deleted, so a cancelled/rescheduled booking's email reminder still fires with no recovery path; console.log should be the project logger

[Medium/bug] handleCancelBooking.ts / bookings.tsx — for EMAIL reminders the DB row is no longer deleted, only marked cancelled, relying on cron query cancelled: true AND scheduledDate <= now+1h; reminders with null scheduledDate or cancelled outside that window will never be picked up and linger

[Low/performance] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:46 — SendGrid cancel requests are awaited sequentially in a for loop every cron tick, risking cron/HTTP timeout with many reminders; also the cancelled + scheduledDate query has no supporting index on WorkflowReminder

[Low/performance] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — cron scans for cancelled: true reminders every run; consider a compound filter (e.g. also scheduled: true) so unscheduled/cancelled-before-scheduling rows aren't repeatedly scanned

[Low/api] workflows.tsx:2-8 — PrismaPromise is imported as a value from @prisma/client; it is a type-only export in current Prisma versions, breaking under isolatedModules/bundlers and inconsistent with removed import type usage

[Low/doc_defect] workflows.tsx:900-960 — a large block has its indentation stripped (misformatted code), indicating accidental editor reformatting in the diff that will fail lint/prettier and hurts reviewability
[Low/test_gap] — no tests cover the new cancellation flow: cancelled flag marking, the cron cancel-within-1h query, immediateDelete behavior, or null-referenceId handling

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:52-56 — reminder.referenceId can be null but is passed directly as SendGrid batch_id, causing a malformed API request that aborts cancellation for subsequent reminders in the loop

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation loop queries reminders only by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate` (no `referenceId` constraint), then calls SendGrid with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`. The diff elsewhere updates `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to accept `referenceId: string | null`, indicating `referenceId` can be null. Passing a null `batch_id` can trigger a request error, and because the whole loop is inside a single `try { ... } catch`, the first such error would jump to `catch` and stop processing remaining reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-67 — if the SendGrid cancel request throws for one reminder, the whole loop aborts via the catch, skipping cancellation/DB deletion of remaining reminders; failed reminders are never marked or retried so the email still sends

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try { ... } catch { ... }`. Inside the loop it `await client.request(...)` before enqueueing the Prisma delete. If SendGrid `client.request` throws for any one reminder, control jumps to the outer `catch`, aborting the loop and skipping cancellation/DB deletion for the remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel`. Those remaining reminders are neither cancelled at SendGrid nor deleted/updated in DB in this run, so the behavior described is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:62 — workflowReminder.delete runs unconditionally right after issuing the async/best-effort SendGrid cancel request, deleting the DB row even if cancellation later fails and the email sends anyway (no reconciliation)

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the DB delete is not run “unconditionally” after a best-effort cancel: the code `await client.request(...)` is awaited inside a try block, and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminder.id } })` promise is only created/pushed if that request completes without throwing. If the SendGrid cancel call fails (throws), execution jumps to `catch` and no delete is issued for that reminder. The claim about “later fails and the email sends anyway / no reconciliation” relies on external SendGrid behavior not shown/verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] emailReminderManager.ts:197 (immediateDelete branch) — reminder is cancelled in SendGrid but the DB row is neither deleted nor marked cancelled, so rows accumulate permanently and the cron query (cancelled: true) never cleans them up

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` has an `immediateDelete` branch that POSTs to SendGrid to cancel the batch and then `return`s without updating or deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row. Call sites now use `immediateDelete: true` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` reschedule cleanup and multiple places in `workflows.tsx`), and the prior `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` deletions were removed in those flows. Also, the new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only selects `where: { cancelled: true }`, so reminders cancelled via the `immediateDelete` branch will never be picked up for deletion/cleanup, leaving DB rows behind (at least for reschedule paths where the booking/reminder isn’t cascade-deleted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] smsReminderManager.ts:178 — if twilio.cancelSMS throws, the catch swallows the error and workflowReminder.delete never executes; reminder stays in DB, SMS may still deliver, no retry mechanism, only a console.log

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts the new deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId) wraps both `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` in a single try/catch. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, execution jumps to the catch and the Prisma delete is skipped, leaving the WorkflowReminder row undeleted. The catch only `console.log`s, so there’s no retry or propagation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] workflows.tsx:572 — remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) fires async cancels without awaiting, so replacement reminders can be scheduled before old ones are cancelled, allowing duplicates; rejections are also unhandled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` the diff introduces `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); });` but the calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are not awaited nor are the resulting promises collected. Since `forEach` doesn't await the async callback, the router continues immediately (and later logic can proceed to update/schedule reminders) before cancels complete; any rejection from the cancel/delete operations is also effectively unhandled. This is a real concurrency/correctness issue visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] emailReminderManager.ts — on any error the function logs via console.log and returns without marking the reminder cancelled or deleted, so a cancelled/rescheduled booking's email reminder still fires with no recovery path; console.log should be the project logger

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` wraps all logic in a `try/catch` and on any error only `console.log(...)`s (no rethrow) and exits without updating the DB (`cancelled: true`) or deleting the reminder. Since the new recovery path in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only cancels reminders where `cancelled: true`, a failure here can leave a scheduled reminder active with no later cleanup indicated by this diff. The note about using the project logger is also supported: this function uses `console.log` rather than the app logger.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] handleCancelBooking.ts / bookings.tsx — for EMAIL reminders the DB row is no longer deleted, only marked cancelled, relying on cron query cancelled: true AND scheduledDate <= now+1h; reminders with null scheduledDate or cancelled outside that window will never be picked up and linger

adjudication.rationale: Diff changes EMAIL cancellation to no longer delete the WorkflowReminder row in most paths. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now either (a) deletes only when `referenceId` is null, or (b) for normal cancellations just `update`s `{ cancelled: true }` and does not cancel the remote send. Cleanup is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only selects `cancelled: true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now+1h` and then cancels + deletes them. Therefore EMAIL reminders with `scheduledDate` null won’t match this query and can linger indefinitely, and cancellations far in advance rely on this periodic job to eventually cancel/delete rather than doing it immediately. This matches the finding (though “outside that window will never be picked up” is only strictly true for null/missing `scheduledDate`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:46 — SendGrid cancel requests are awaited sequentially in a for loop every cron tick, risking cron/HTTP timeout with many reminders; also the cancelled + scheduledDate query has no supporting index on WorkflowReminder

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the new cancellation block iterates `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` and `await`s `client.request(...)` inside the loop, making SendGrid cancels run sequentially (diff shows an `await` per iteration before collecting delete promises). That can become slow as reminder count grows. The new query filters on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= ...`, but the migration only adds the `cancelled` column (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN;`) and the Prisma schema adds `cancelled Boolean?` with no index defined/added in this diff, so the “no supporting index” concern is diff-grounded. This is a performance/maintainability concern rather than a definite correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — cron scans for cancelled: true reminders every run; consider a compound filter (e.g. also scheduled: true) so unscheduled/cancelled-before-scheduling rows aren't repeatedly scanned

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the new cron query scans `WorkflowReminder` rows with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h` but does not further narrow by `scheduled` (even though the model has a `scheduled Boolean`). If any cancelled rows exist that aren’t actually scheduled (or otherwise shouldn’t be processed), they’ll still be included in the scan each run. Adding an additional predicate such as `scheduled: true` (or `referenceId: { not: null }`) would make the query more selective and reduce unnecessary scanning/work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] workflows.tsx:2-8 — PrismaPromise is imported as a value from @prisma/client; it is a type-only export in current Prisma versions, breaking under isolatedModules/bundlers and inconsistent with removed import type usage

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the diff changes `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise } from "@prisma/client";` to a value import `import { PrismaPromise, ... , Prisma } from "@prisma/client";` (lines 1-12). `PrismaPromise` is only used as a TypeScript annotation in this file, so importing it as a runtime value can cause TS/isolatedModules/verbatimModuleSyntax builds (and some bundlers) to error because it’s a type-only export in modern Prisma/TS setups. This is a diff-grounded, potentially build-breaking defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] workflows.tsx:900-960 — a large block has its indentation stripped (misformatted code), indicating accidental editor reformatting in the diff that will fail lint/prettier and hurts reviewability

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a large block in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` where indentation was removed (lines around the shown `if (isSMSAction(step.action)...)` and subsequent object literals). However, this is a formatting/style concern only; the code remains syntactically valid in the diff, and whether it will “fail lint/prettier” is not verifiable from the diff alone. Under the given categories, pure formatting nits fall under hallucination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] — no tests cover the new cancellation flow: cancelled flag marking, the cron cancel-within-1h query, immediateDelete behavior, or null-referenceId handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new cancellation behavior (e.g., `WorkflowReminder.cancelled` column + update path in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, null-`referenceId` deletion, `immediateDelete` branch, and a new “cancel within next hour” query/cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`). The PR diff shows no corresponding test additions/updates exercising these branches (no test files changed), so lack of coverage for these new flows is a specific, diff-grounded review gap rather than a functional defect by itself.
